tryThisNow: Open a shared spreadsheet and add three columns before keeping any bargain candidate: low P/E group, net-net test, and 20-stock group slot.

implementationPlan.title: Build a Bargain Screen Friction Check
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Turn bargain selection into a repeatable screen before any candidate stays active. Start with low P/E groups, test net-net candidates against current assets minus all liabilities, and keep the decision tied to a 20-stock group instead of one favorite bargain.

ifThenPlans.plan: If Julian wants to keep a low P/E candidate after a manager one-on-one, then he adds a low P/E group row and checks financial condition before treating cheapness as favorable odds.
If Tessa calls a candidate net-net during a phone call, then she pauses until market price has been compared with current assets minus all liabilities.
If Samir is tempted to concentrate in 1 cheap company in the shared spreadsheet, then he marks the 20-stock group slot first and leaves the candidate pending until group diversification is visible.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before the next day ends, create one shared spreadsheet row for a current bargain candidate. Leave it pending unless the row shows low P/E group status, net-net comparison, and the 20-stock group slot.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Use one recurring conversation each week to review the shared spreadsheet. Keep only candidates with a low P/E group note, a net-net comparison when claimed, and a visible place inside the 20-stock group.
